notices.title: Notice of Justice Court Vacancy
notices.agenda_text:
JUSTICE COURT VACANCY ANNOUNCED FOR LEHI 

Applications are being accepted for a full-time justice court judge position that will serve Lehi, Utah. The successful candidate will replace Judge Morgan Cummings who will resign his position in October. 

To be considered for a justice court judgeship in Utah County, candidates must be at least 25 years of age, a citizen of the United States, a Utah resident for at least three years, and have a degree from a law school that would make one eligible to apply for admission to a bar in any state in the United States. In addition, applicants must be a resident of Utah County or an adjacent county either upon appointment or before taking the bench. 

To be considered for this position, an application for judicial office must be completed online at justicecourtvacancies.utah.gov before the deadline. The salary range for the position is $147,886 to $190,139 per year and includes benefits. For additional information about working for Lehi, contact David Kitchen, the Human Resources Manager for Lehi, at (385) 201-2265 or dkitchen@lehiut.gov.  The deadline for applications is Friday, October 9, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Applications cannot be submitted after the deadline. For questions about the justice courts or the process for filling this position, email Jim Peters, Justice Court Administrator, at jamesp@utcourts.gov. 

Utah law requires the Judicial Nominating Commission to submit at least three nominees to Mayor Paul Binns within 45 days of its first meeting. Mayor Binns will then have 30 days in which to select a finalist. His selection must then be ratified by the Lehi City Council and certified by the Utah Judicial Council.

notices.title: Lehi City Planning Commission Public Hearing Items
notices.agenda_text:
LEHI CITY PLANNING COMMISSION NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING


On September 10, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. in the Lehi Civic Center Council Chambers located at 131 North 100 East, the Lehi City Planning Commission will hold a public hearing to receive public comment on the following items:

Public hearing and consideration of Adam Albrecht's request for approval of an exception for the Garden Park Subdivision, revising a 6-foot no climb fence along the railroad corridor to be an 8-foot wall located at approximately 500 S Center Street. 
 
Public hearing and consideration of AT&T's request for conditional use approval of the AT&T River Walk Preliminary Children's Antenna, requesting to place a telecommunications antenna on top of Primary Children's Hospital located at 2250 North Miller Campus Drive. 
 
Public hearing and consideration of Alpine Bible Church's request for approval of an exception for the Alpine Bible Church located at 710 West Main Street requesting an exception to the glass requirement. 
 
Public hearing and recommendation of Lehi City's request for review of the Chapter 29 Development Code Amendment, clarifying the development agreement process.

Public hearing and consideration of Uncommon Architecture's request for approval of exceptions to the Outlets at Traverse Mountain Storage Building's architectural requirements including maximum EIFS percentages, architectural features, and glass requirements located at 3800 Cabela's Boulevard.

notices.agenda_text:
July 14, 2026
Lehi City
Public Hearing Notice
Impact Fee Enactment

Notice is hereby given that Lehi City intends to adopt an Impact Fee Enactment Ordinance, Impact Fee Facilities Plan and Impact Fee Analysis for the provision of public safety facilities within Lehi City. The Lehi City Council will hold a public hearing on Tuesday, July 28, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. at Lehi City Hall in the Council Chambers, 131 N 100 E, Lehi, Utah. The purpose of the public hearing is to receive input and consider approval and adoption of the Impact Fee Enactment Ordinance, Impact Fee Facilities Plan, and Impact Fee Analysis. All interested persons shall be given the opportunity to be heard. Written comments are welcome.

Copies of the Impact Fee Enactment Ordinance, Impact Fee Facilities Plan, and Impact Fee Analysis are available for public review at the Lehi City Office or by contacting the City Recorder, twilson@lehi-ut.gov; 385-201-2269. In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, the city will make reasonable accommodations to participants in the hearing. Requests for assistance can be made by calling 385-201-2269 at least 48 hours in advance of the hearing.
